title: Lazar's 'gravity wave A' may be a garbled QCD theta term / Chern-Simons

tellings.quote: Is it possible, Eric, that what he's talking about is that the theta term from QCD is what he's calling stupidly gravity wave A, which no person I've ever heard of has ever used that terminology.

plain: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien spacecraft at a secret site near Area 51 in Nevada in 1989, described a force he called "gravity wave A", and a researcher named Eric Weinstein wonders whether this could be a mangled name for a real idea from physics. Weinstein asks whether Lazar meant the "theta term", a piece of the mathematics of the theory of the strong nuclear force, or a related mathematical structure called Chern-Simons, noting that nobody he knows of has ever used the phrase "gravity wave A". If so, it would mean Lazar was repeating real but advanced physics he had only half understood.
